chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'When a man strikes a woman and she drops the seed,' he said, 'Upon him is twenty Dinars. So if it was a clot, then upon him is forty Dinars; and if it was a lump, then upon him is sixty Dinars; and if it was bones, then upon him is the wergild.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for miscarriage caused by striking a pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a graduated system of blood money (diyah) for miscarriage caused by physical trauma, reflecting the Shia juristic view that fetal value increases with developmental stages. It highlights the distinction between fixed monetary penalties for early stages (seed, clot, lump) and the full adult wergild once bones are formed, a principle widely cited in Shia fiqh for calculating compensation in cases of accidental or intentional harm.
